messages:
andrew.k: Quick design Q: we're reworking envelope flow for customer-pii. Questions: 1) Should DEKs be per-tenant or per-object? 2) KMS call frequency—do we call KMS per-request for unwrap, or cache DEKs? 3) What RBAC/audit controls do we need for KEK unwraps? 4) Rotation playbook? TL;DR: want safe defaults before we land on perf tradeoffs.

maria.p: Short answers: 1) per-tenant DEK is usually fine unless customers need per-object audit. 2) Cache DEKs in memory with strict TTL + LRU, avoid per-request KMS. 3) KMS principals should be minimal (Decrypt only), use KMS condition on requester service principal. 4) Rotation: rewrap asynchronously + dual-write for a window.

samir.t: Additions: - Keep cache TTL tied to key-rotation window: TTL << rotation interval. - Use envelope metadata: key_id, kek_version, wrapped_at for audits. - For hotkeys, use local in-process cache + fallback to shared cache (redis) for warmup.

security-bot: Note: AWS recommends calling KMS to Decrypt when you can't securely store plaintext DEKs. Caching is allowed but must be justified in threat model. See https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/envelope-keys.html :thumbsup:

maria.p: Example cache policy we use in other services:
```
cache:
  type: local+shared
  local_ttl_sec: 300   # 5 minutes
  shared_ttl_sec: 3600 # 1 hour
  max_entries: 5000
  revalidate_before: 30 # seconds before local expiry, async refresh
```

andrew.k: Do we have numbers on KMS QPS cost? I want ballpark for peak 10k req/s.

samir.t: Ballpark: 10k unwraps/sec -> really expensive on KMS and latency. Cache reduces KMS QPS by orders of magnitude. Consider batching rewraps and async re-encryption during rotation rather than on-request.

maria.p: RBAC: - Service principal role: kms:Decrypt + kms:Encrypt on KEK resource only. - Use separate role for ops that can trigger rotation and view audit logs. - Deny iam:PassRole for untrusted agents.

oncall-ops: Incident notes: If KEK compromised (KMS key compromised or IAM leak): 1) revoke key policy and rotate KEK, 2) mark all DEKs as potentially exposed, kick off rewrap job, 3) rotate downstream tokens, 4) notify legal/compliance per SLA. Keep runbook steps concise.

samir.t: A couple more specifics: - For multi-cloud: store kek_ref with cloud/provider tag (aws:kms:arn, gcp:cryptoKeyName). - For GCP, use EKM or CloudKMS; ensure audit logs forwarded to BigQuery/SIEM. - For Azure Key Vault, same pattern: store key id and version in envelope metadata.

maria.p: Audit logging guidance: - Log every KEK wrap/unwrap with principal, key_version, request_id, operation, latency. - Send KMS audit events + application-level envelope events to central SIEM. - Retain for at least 1 year for enterprise customers; longer if required by contract.

andrew.k: Example envelope record we could store in DB:
```
{
  "object_id": "...",
  "dek_wrapped": "base64(...)",
  "kek_ref": "arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd:1",
  "kek_version": "v1",
  "wrapped_at": "2025-03-05T12:34:56Z"
}
```

security-bot: Tip: For rotation, do "wrap new DEKs with new KEK version" then atomically flip pointer to new kek_version. Keep old KEK available for unwrap until rewrap completes.

maria.p: Threat model note: caching plaintext DEKs increases blast radius. Mitigation: encrypt in-process memory via OS protections (mprotect + guard pages), short TTL, and rotate process creds frequently.

andrew.k: OK thanks—can someone put a short proposal + config defaults in a RFC? I'll volunteer to draft.

maria.p: I'll review. tagging @samir.t and @oncall-ops for ops/runbook.

oncall-ops: got it, I'll add incident steps to the runbook and a checklist for rotation drills.

security-bot: /remind #eng-security in 3d to review RFC draft
